solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Musical theatre that’s old has Europe excited (5,5)

indicatorNotes.excited: excited letters are stirred up out of their calm order

annotation.surface: A dusty old theatre gets the whole continent in a flutter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's old' reads as a description of the theatre, but it only supplies the single letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the building takes its name from the sung drama staged there, so 'musical theatre' names it by what it houses.

entries.clue: Pained expression, in a sense — tee off (4)

indicatorNotes.off: the tee comes off, so T is taken away

blocks.note: touch is one of the five senses
tee is the sound of the letter T, spelt out as a word; removed

annotation.surface: A golfer winces as they tee off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tee off' sounds like the start of a golf round; here tee is the letter T and off tells you to drop it from TOUCH.
annotation.definitionFit: Ouch is what you say when something hurts.

entries.clue: Surprised reaction for one piece of publicity (4)

annotation.surface: Someone is startled by a single advertisement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' is a common crossword way of asking for E.G.
annotation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise.

entries.clue: Everyone repeating what cryptic crossword creator is doing (12)

annotation.definition: what cryptic crossword creator is doing
annotation.surface: Everyone keeps repeating what the setter is up to.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: the three words 'cryptic crossword creator' all begin with C, so whoever wrote them is alliterating.
annotation.definitionFit: Stringing words with the same opening sound, as 'cryptic crossword creator' does, is alliterating.

entries.clue: Start of attack where crew does some shooting (5)

blocks.note: the first moment of an assault or of an illness
a film crew shoots on the studio stage, two words run together

annotation.surface: An assault opens where soldiers are firing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' and 'attack' suggest a battle; the shooting is filming, and split as ON SET the answer is where a film crew works.
annotation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning, especially of something hostile or unpleasant.

entries.clue: Locality’s rebuilt without complaint (9)

indicatorNotes.rebuilt: rebuilt letters are put together in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A neighbourhood is reconstructed and nobody grumbles.
annotation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is part of the fodder, which is easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: To bear something stoically is to endure it without complaint.

entries.clue: Force everyone to yield to temptation (4)

annotation.surface: Someone compels a whole group to give in to temptation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as a verb governing the rest; it is just the abbreviation F.
annotation.definitionFit: To fall is to sin or give way to temptation, as in the Fall of Adam and Eve.

entries.clue: Pupil at easel in a depression about broken trust (3,7)

indicatorNotes.about: a dent goes about, surrounding, the other letters
indicatorNotes.broken: broken letters are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: A + DENT, a depression; it wraps around the next piece after its first letter

annotation.surface: A painting pupil is down in the dumps because their trust has been betrayed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' and 'broken trust' paint a mood; the depression is a dent, as in a bumped car.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by picture: the easel is the tool of a painter, so a pupil standing at one is learning art.

entries.clue: Less than grand achievement for couple holding hands (6,4)

annotation.definition: Less than grand achievement for couple holding hands

blocks.note: reads as a modest success; in bridge a grand slam is taking all thirteen tricks, so this is the contract one step below
reads as sweethearts; in bridge the couple is a partnership and the hands are hands of cards

annotation.surface: A courting couple, hand in hand, manage something modest.
annotation.walkthrough: The couple are bridge partners and the hands are hands of cards; 'grand' points to the grand slam, all thirteen tricks.
annotation.definitionFit: A little slam is the bridge contract just below the grand slam, made by a partnership.

entries.clue: Personification of majesty and style in old dance (10)

annotation.surface: A dignified figure shows grace in a period dance.
annotation.walkthrough: TON for style is an old borrowing from French, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by period: the Charleston was the craze of the 1920s, so 'old dance' is fair.

entries.clue: Is, at best, deficient in odd places? Don’t try to improve it (4)

indicatorNotes.deficient in odd places: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters go missing, leaving the even ones

annotation.surface: Something that is merely adequate at its best should be left alone.
annotation.walkthrough: Stet is the proofreader's instruction 'let it stand', cancelling a correction.
annotation.definitionFit: Stet tells the printer to leave the text as it was.

entries.clue: Representative thrusts a child under spotlight initially (12)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer, what is under comes after

blocks.note: a = per, as in 'ten pounds a head'

annotation.surface: A delegate shoves a youngster into the glare of attention.
annotation.walkthrough: The little word 'a' does real work here, as PER.
annotation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of, and so represents, others.

entries.clue: Important city’s condition — excellent (5,7)

annotation.surface: A report on a major city: its condition is excellent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City's' reads as a possessive; the 's stands for 'is'. Capital as a cry of approval is old-fashioned British English.
annotation.definitionFit: A state capital is the seat of government of a state, a city of importance.

entries.clue: Vague, unreflective thinking involving endless depression (10)

indicatorNotes.involving: instinct takes in, involves, the other piece
indicatorNotes.endless: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: instinct is thought without reflection; it wraps around the next piece after IN
DIP, a depression, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Hazy, knee-jerk thought when someone is a bit low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood; it is a dip in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Indistinct means vague, not clearly defined.

entries.clue: Critical mood, in a manner of speaking (10)

annotation.definition2: mood, in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: critical in the sense of vitally important, not fault-finding

blocks.clueFragment: mood, in a manner of speaking
blocks.note: a grammatical mood, the verb form used for commands

annotation.surface: A disapproving frame of mind, so to speak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge ('so to speak'); it literally points to grammar, a way of speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: Imperative means essential, and is also the verb mood used for orders.

entries.clue: I’m unclear about particular type of data (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are moved about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone admits confusion over a certain kind of information.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unclear' looks like the anagram indicator, but it belongs in the fodder; 'about' does the stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: figures are one kind of data, as opposed to text or categories.

entries.clue: Map change altered French region (9)

indicatorNotes.altered: altered letters are changed into another order

annotation.surface: A redrawn map shifts the borders of a French province.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is cartography, which makes 'region' look like a matter of boundaries rather than a place name.
annotation.definitionFit: Champagne is a region of north-east France, home of the wine.

entries.clue: Pessimistic lawmaker this country backed for prestigious recognition (5)

indicatorNotes.backed: backed means turned back to front

blocks.note: Sod's law says whatever can go wrong will, so Sod made the pessimistic law
from a British newspaper, this country is the UK

annotation.surface: A gloomy legislator is supported by the nation for an honour.
annotation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British name for Murphy's law; 'lawmaker' wants to be a politician, but it is whoever the law is named after.
annotation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and prestige earned by an achievement.

entries.clue: Bumbling or inexpert, discarding ten and queen (5)

blocks.note: the word itself, before the removals
X is the Roman numeral ten, removed
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, removed

annotation.surface: A clumsy card player throws away the ten and queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discarding ten and queen' sounds like a card game; the ten is X and the queen ER, both lifted out of INEXPERT.
annotation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and incompetent, as a bumbler is.

entries.clue: Old part of Africa with chasm in one area (9)

annotation.surface: A former African territory has a deep gorge in one of its districts.
annotation.walkthrough: The small word that looks like a container instruction is simply used as itself, so the clue reads straight off left to right.
annotation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia.

entries.clue: Enthusiast engaged in on-line recording? (12)

blocks.note: a hobbyist, a fan of some pastime
reads as internet activity; the line is a railway line, and the recording is writing down locomotive numbers

annotation.surface: An internet hobbyist busy with streaming or podcasting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On-line' suggests the internet; the line is a railway line. Trainspotting is a classically British hobby of logging locomotive numbers.
annotation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is an enthusiast who records the trains they see.

entries.clue: From perspective of team game, second form lacking centre (5)

blocks.note: as in 'to me, it looks wrong'

annotation.surface: Seen from a sports team's angle, the second formation has no one in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lacking centre' looks like a deletion instruction, but it belongs to the definition: a torus is a ring with a hole where its centre would be.
annotation.definitionFit: A torus is a doughnut-shaped solid, a form with an empty middle.

entries.clue: In hearing, represent part of body (4)

indicatorNotes.In hearing: what is heard is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: to limn is to depict or portray; its final N is silent

annotation.surface: At a court hearing, someone acts for a body.
annotation.walkthrough: LIMN is an uncommon word meaning to draw or portray; both it and LIMB have a silent final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the general level: arms and legs are the body parts meant.

entries.clue: Solo appearance in concert (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit between the C and the RT of concert

annotation.surface: A soloist takes a turn on stage at a concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solo appearance' sounds like a performance; it means a single occurrence.
annotation.definitionFit: Once means on one occasion only, a single appearance.

entries.clue: Catch something that’s over quick (4)

blocks.note: catch as in apprehend a culprit, informal
the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail

annotation.surface: Grab something that's done in no time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as fast; it is the noun, the sensitive skin a fingernail covers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the informal verb for collaring someone, and the horny plate on a fingertip that covers the quick.

entries.clue: Organises, having regrouped around leader of gang, for hostile action (10)

indicatorNotes.having regrouped: regrouped letters are put into new groupings
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters surround the G
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of gang, held inside

annotation.surface: A gang boss rallies his followers for an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of ORGANISES goes around G; the letters settle as A + G + G(RESSION), with the gang's G one of the pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unprovoked attack or hostile behaviour.

entries.clue: Specifically, which letter winds up litigation in that case (4)

indicatorNotes.winds up: the letter that winds up a word is the one it ends with

blocks.note: the, stressed, singles out one thing, as in 'THE place to eat'

annotation.surface: A lawyer asks exactly which letter closes a lawsuit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Specifically' is a loose but fair route to THE, the definite article used to single one thing out.
annotation.definitionFit: Then means in that case, as in 'if so, then go'.

entries.clue: Fit for winter, say, as one cycles wearing fur (10)

indicatorNotes.cycles: letters cycle when the front ones move round to the back
indicatorNotes.wearing: the fur is worn around the other piece

blocks.note: sable is a prized fur; it wraps around the next piece after its S
ASONE with its last letter E cycled round to the front

annotation.surface: Wrapped in fur, a cyclist is ready for the cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winter, say' is an example of a season, so seasonable means suited to the season; 'cycles' is not about bicycles.
annotation.definitionFit: Seasonable means suited to the time of year, as warm clothes are in winter.
